focus: /aʊ/ (house) vs /əʊ/ (home) · /uː/ (room) vs /ʊ/ (book) · unstressed /ɪ/ (kitchen) · silent letters (two, know) · /w/ vs /v/ (window, very)
focus_ar: /aʊ/ مقابل /əʊ/، و /uː/ مقابل /ʊ/، و /ɪ/ غير المنبورة، والحروف الصامتة، و /w/ مقابل /v/
arabic_challenge: Arabic has no /əʊ/ or /aʊ/ as single gliding vowels, so 'house' and 'home' get flattened. Arabic /w/ exists but learners often merge English /w/ and /v/. Silent letters (two, know, write) are purely a spelling trap.

isolation.instructions: /aʊ/ (house) starts wide open like /æ/ and glides to /ʊ/ — jaw closes, lips round. /əʊ/ (home) starts in the middle and glides to /ʊ/ — lips round from earlier. Both MOVE; neither is a single flat vowel.
isolation.instructions_ar: /aʊ/ يبدأ مفتوح وينتهي بشفاه مدوّرة. /əʊ/ يبدأ من النص وينتهي مدوّر. الاتنين أصوات متحركة مش ثابتة.

sentence_practice: My house is in the old town.
The phone is on the sofa.
daily_drills.record_this: My house is in the old town. I go home now and the phone is on the sofa near the window.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'now' and 'no'. Does your jaw clearly move for both — and do they sound different from each other?

isolation.instructions: /uː/ (room, two) is LONG with tightly rounded, pushed-forward lips. /ʊ/ (book, good) is SHORT with relaxed, barely-rounded lips. Length and tension both matter.
isolation.instructions_ar: /uː/ طويل والشفاه مدوّرة ومدفوعة للأمام. /ʊ/ قصير والشفاه مسترخية. الفرق في الطول والشد.

sentence_practice: There are two rooms and one bathroom.
I cook food in the kitchen.
daily_drills.record_this: There are two rooms and one bathroom in my house. Look at the good book on the bookshelf. I cook food in the kitchen.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'fool' then 'full'. Are your lips tighter and the sound longer for the first one?

isolation.instructions: In long words, only ONE syllable is strong; the rest shrink. KIT-chen, GAR-den, BUILD-ing, FUR-ni-ture. The weak syllables become a tiny /ɪ/ or /ə/ — do not give every syllable equal weight.
isolation.instructions_ar: في الكلمات الطويلة مقطع واحد بس قوي والباقي يتقلّص: KIT-chen، GAR-den. المقاطع الخفيفة تبقى صوت صغير جدًا — مش كل مقطع بنفس القوة.

sentence_practice: The kitchen is next to the living room.
There is a garden behind the building.
daily_drills.record_this: The kitchen is next to the living room. There is a small garden behind the building, and my apartment has new furniture.
daily_drills.self_check: Tap the table only on the STRONG syllable. Should be one tap per word, not two or three.

isolation.instructions: Some letters are written but never spoken: two (no /w/), know/knife (no /k/), write (no /w/), hour (no /h/), walk/talk (no /l/), half (no /l/), listen (no /t/). Say the word, not the spelling.
isolation.instructions_ar: في حروف تُكتب ولا تُنطق: two (بدون w)، know (بدون k)، write (بدون w)، hour (بدون h)، walk (بدون l). انطق الكلمة مش الإملاء.

sentence_practice: I know there are two rooms.
daily_drills.record_this: I know there are two rooms in this house. I walk for half an hour every day. Please listen and do not talk.
daily_drills.self_check: Does 'know' sound exactly like 'no'? It should.

isolation.instructions: /w/ = both lips round and push forward, NO teeth involved (like Arabic و). /v/ = top TEETH touch the bottom lip. If your teeth touch your lip for 'window', it is wrong.
isolation.instructions_ar: /w/ الشفاه مدوّرة للأمام والأسنان مش مشاركة (زي و). /v/ الأسنان العليا تلمس الشفة السفلى. لو أسنانك لمست شفتك في 'window' يبقى غلط.

sentence_practice: The window is in the wall.
We live in a very small village.
daily_drills.record_this: The window is in the wall next to the wardrobe. We live in a very small village and I walk to the water every evening.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'window' — your teeth must NOT touch your lip. Then say 'very' — they must.

challenge_sentences: My house has two bedrooms and a kitchen.
Look out of the window at the garden.
I know we live in a very old town.
Walk home now — it is half an hour.
daily_drills.record_this: My house has two bedrooms and a kitchen. Look out of the window at the garden. I know we live in a very old town, so walk home now — it takes half an hour.
daily_drills.self_check: Check three things: do 'now/no' differ, is 'two' free of any /w/, and do your teeth stay off your lip for /w/?

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself describing a home. Then listen back and check each sound group.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت توصف بيت، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل مجموعة أصوات.
test_yourself.passage: This is my house. It is in a small town, not in the city. There are two bedrooms, one bathroom and a big living room. The kitchen is next to the living room, and there is a garden behind the house. I look out of the window every morning. We have new furniture and a good bookshelf full of books. I know it is old, but I love my home. It takes half an hour to walk into town.

sounds_to_check./aʊ/ vs /əʊ/: house, town, out, now, around — home, go, no, window, sofa, old
sounds_to_check./uː/ vs /ʊ/: two, room, bathroom, food — book, look, good, full, bookshelf
sounds_to_check.silent letters: two, know, walk, half, hour, listen
sounds_to_check./w/ vs /v/: window, wall, walk, we — very, living, have, love

scoring_guide.90_100: Gliding vowels clearly move, /w/ and /v/ never merge. Ready for week 5.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasional flattening of /əʊ/ or a slipped silent letter.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, using the mirror to watch your lips move on the gliding vowels.

for_arabic_speakers: /aʊ/ and /əʊ/ are MOVING vowels. If your mouth stays still, the word will sound wrong.
Long vs short /uː/-/ʊ/ changes meaning (fool/full). Arabic vowel length does not work the same way.
/w/ uses lips only. Never let the teeth touch the lip — that turns 'window' into 'vindow'.
Silent letters are a spelling trap, not a pronunciation choice: 'two' is simply 'too'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily and compare day 7 with day 1.
